communications.subject: Colorado Open Records Act Request: Gunnison ALPR locations
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Colorado Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All fixed ALPR locations in Gunnison County leased, ordered, monitored, operated, or associated with the Gunnison County Sheriff’s Office.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

William Beckett

Invoice Number: INV26-C246559-1 
Total: $1.25 
 
To pay online, please follow these steps: 
 Please note that you will need to disable any pop-up blockers to make a payment using the system. 
 
  * Navigate to the Public Records Request Center.
  * Select 'My Records Request Center'. 
  * Select 'View My Requests'. You may be asked to login. 
  * Find this request: C246559-111525. 
  * Select the 'View Invoices' button. 
 
  * Opens a pop-up window showing your invoice: INV26-C246559-1. 
  * Click on the invoice and then the 'Pay Now' button. 
  * Continue processing your payment. 
  * Select 'Done'. 
  * Once the payment process is done, you are returned to the Public Records Request Center. 
  * After your payment is successful you will receive an email from our payments center. 
Once your payment has been approved, we will send you an email with instructions on how to download your records. Note that City staff must manually upload records. Records will be available one to two business days after payment. 
 
Please let your public disclosure officer (PDO) know if you are unable to pay online; your PDO will work with you on alternative ways to make your payment. 
 
You have 30 days from today's date to pay for your records. If the City does not receive your payment within this time period, your request will be considered abandoned, and you will need to submit a new request.

communications.subject: DC Freedom of Information Act Request: The "Discussed Ditch" Cover-Up: Exposing DC's 25-Foot Ward 8 Landslide
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

To: ddot.foia@dc.gov
CC: eugene.adams@dc.gov; molc.mayor@dc.gov; foia.appeals@dc.gov; tnorflis@dccouncil.gov; rmckinney@dccouncil.gov
Subject: FOIA Request: DDOT Arborist Inspection Logs, Unannounced Site Visits, & Cross-Agency Referrals (1490 Morris Rd SE)

To the District Department of Transportation (DDOT) FOIA Officer:

Under the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq.), I am formally requesting copies of the following public records pertaining to the property and public right-of-way located at 1490 Morris Rd SE, Washington, DC 20020. This request includes, but is not limited to, records tied to 311 Service Request #26-00495403, as well as any internally directed, unscheduled, or ad-hoc site visits. 

Please provide the following records generated between August 19, 2026, and today's date, September 2, 2026:

1. All internal arborist inspection notes, field reports, work orders, and photographs taken by DDOT Urban Forestry Division (UFD) personnel or contractors during any physical site visit to 1490 Morris Rd SE (including visits allegedly conducted for "tree trimming" or visual assessment).
2. All internal DDOT email communications, dispatch logs, GPS telematics, and routing metadata discussing the condition of the trees, the soil, the slope, or the authorization of a site visit to this location.
3. All cross-agency referrals, notifications, or memoranda sent by DDOT personnel to the Department of Buildings (DOB), the Department of Energy and Environment (DOEE), or the Office of Unified Communications (OUC) regarding the 25-foot slope failure/landslide observed at this location. 

Because the DDOT Urban Forestry Division physically assessed the property but lacks the geotechnical jurisdiction to abate a 25-foot structural landslide, the internal referrals transferring this life-safety hazard to the appropriate structural authorities (DOB/DOEE) are highly relevant to public safety and current oversight investigations.

I request these records be produced in their native electronic format. I am requesting a fee waiver as this request is in the public interest and is actively contributing to public understanding of District infrastructure and hazard response protocols in Ward 8.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

communications.subject: DC Freedom of Information Act Request: FOIA: DDOT Urban Forestry "Ghost Inspections," Metadata & Unmitigated Landslide Hazards (311 Ticket #26-00495403) (District Department of Transportation)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

To: ddot.foia@dc.gov; ouc.foia@dc.gov

CC: callen@dccouncil.gov; pmendelson@dccouncil.us; twhite@dccouncil.gov; ian.maggard@dc.gov; frank.seales@dc.gov; earl.eutsler@dc.gov; david.dickman@dc.gov; ldonovan@wusa9.com; chernande1@wusa9.com

Subject: FOIA REQUEST: 311 Service Request #26-00495403, Urban Forestry Site Metadata, and Imminent Danger Exception (1600-1490 Morris Rd SE)
To the Designated Freedom of Information Act Officers:

Pursuant to the D.C. Freedom of Information Act, I request all records, inspection logs, arborist notes, photographs, owner notification records, and device logs associated with 311 Service Request #26-00495403. Under D.C. Official Code § 2-532(a-1), I specifically demand that all responsive electronic records—especially digital photographs, GPS tracking data, and field logs—be produced in their native electronic format with all original metadata completely intact and unaltered. 

This request explicitly seeks to verify whether a physical site visit was actually conducted or if the Urban Forestry Division improperly relied on stale documentation to close out an urgent safety hazard. Please provide the full identification of the arborist who handled this request, including their full name, title, badge or employee identification number, and any associated field notes. Furthermore, this request seeks to verify whether the DC Urban Forester fulfilled their statutory duty under District arboricultural regulations to formally notify the property owner on record regarding an active life-safety hazard. The trees in question are actively failing, uprooting, and sliding down the public right-of-way, triggering the mandatory Imminent Danger Exception which requires public safety flagging, barricades, or an emergency abatement order rather than administrative dismissal via a "private property" loophole. 

Additionally, this 311 ticket and its mishandling do not exist in a vacuum; they represent a direct symptom of the larger, systemic municipal infrastructure failure. The structural collapse and severe soil erosion threatening these mature trees result from the complete absence of engineered stormwater management. This water originates at the crest of 1600 Morris Rd SE and flows unchecked down the unimproved paper alley corridor to 2258 Hunter Pl SE. 

Fee Waiver Request: Pursuant to D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b), I request a full fee waiver for this request. Disclosure of this information is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of municipal infrastructure failures, environmental safety hazards, and agency compliance with District law. The requester has no commercial interest in the disclosure of these records and is acting in the capacity of a community advocate and public watchdog.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

communications.communication:

Subject: D.C. FOIA REQUEST: Expedited - Unredacted Urban Forestry Assessment, Intact Metadata & GPS Telemetry (1490 Morris Rd SE)

To the District Department of Transportation (DDOT) FOIA Officer,

Pursuant to the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Code § 2-531 et seq.), I am formally requesting copies of the following public records:

1. The complete, unredacted field report, assessment, and all preliminary or finalized inspector notes generated from the DDOT Urban Forestry Division site visit to 1490 Morris Road SE conducted on the afternoon of August 17, 2026.
2. All original, unaltered photograph and video files taken during this August 17, 2026 site visit. These files must be provided in their native digital formats (e.g., raw JPEG, HEIC) with all original EXIF data and metadata fully intact, including timestamps, GPS coordinates, and camera orientation.
3. All internal communications (including emails, text messages, and direct messages) between the assigned urban forester, Earl Eutsler, Director Sharon Kershbaum, the other two unnamed urban foresters, and any other DDOT staff regarding the findings of this specific site visit.
4. All GPS telemetry data, Automated Vehicle Location (AVL) tracking logs, and routing records for the government-issued vehicle assigned to the responding urban forester on August 17, 2026.
5. All call logs, SMS transmission records, and location data associated with the government-issued cellular device used by the responding urban forester on August 17, 2026.

The glaring omission of the 75-year-old Heritage White Oak and the active landslide from the provided photographs raises serious questions about the legitimacy, scope, and duration of yesterday's purported site visit. Obtaining the forester's GPS vehicle telemetry and government-issued cellular data will definitively confirm exactly how much time was actually spent on-site, what exact perimeter was walked, and whether a comprehensive inspection of this imminent life-safety hazard was genuinely conducted—or if this was merely a brief "drive-by" assessment designed to deflect liability and quickly close a ticket.

FEE WAIVER REQUEST: 
I request a complete waiver of all fees associated with processing this request. The disclosure of this information is in the public interest as it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations and activities of the government regarding an unmitigated, active landslide posing a direct life-safety threat to a documented student pedestrian route. This request is not for commercial purposes.

MANDATORY PRESERVATION AND PUBLICATION NOTICE:
Be advised that I have submitted this request, and will upload all resulting agency disclosures, directly to MuckRock.com. This ensures complete transparency and allows investigative journalists, the D.C. Council, and the public to monitor DDOT's compliance. Any attempt to scrub metadata or withhold raw files will be documented on the public record. 

Given the imminent life-safety threat to the DC Prep student route as the academic year begins today, I request expedited processing. 

Respectfully,

Fred Gamble Jr.
1490 Morris Rd SE
Fort Stanton Neighbors
Washington, DC 20020
(301) 651-8904

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

To: Marcus Greer
P. O. Box 310
Carnesville, GA 30521

mgreer@franklincosheriff.net
Phone: 706-384-2525

Public reports state that this county is using cameras from Flock Safety (a.k.a. "Flock"), the automatic license plate reader (ALPR) company. For the purposes of this request, when I refer to "Flock products," this includes hardware (Flock License Plate Readers (LPRs), Flock Safety Falcons, Flock Video Cameras, Flock Mobile Security Trailers, Flock Gunshot and Audio Detection Devices, Flock Drone as First Responder (DFRs), and Flock Alpha) as well as software (Flock Safety Platform, FlockOS, Flock911, Flock Nova, Flock FreeForm, Flock Vehicle Fingerprint technology, and the National LPR Network). Source:
https://www.flocksafety.com/products
Therefore, pursuant to Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records (dated September 19, 2026 to the time this request is processed):
1. All contracts, purchase orders, invoices, receipts, payment records, budgetary quotes, and related procurement records involving Flock Safety.
2. All training, instructional, presentation, and guidance materials concerning the use of any Flock Safety product or service, including hardware and software. This includes, but is not limited to:
a) Presentations, videos, audio recordings, scripts, manuals, and training materials;
b) Meeting notes discussing the use of Flock products;
c) Technical or operational explanations of how Flock products function; and
d) Internal or external documents used to explain, train on, or promote the use of Flock products.
3. All policies, procedures, agreements, and legal documents relating to Flock Safety or its products, including terms and conditions, privacy impact assessments, standard operating procedures, use policies, data retention policies, legal opinions, warranties, nondisclosure agreements, memoranda of understanding, liability waivers, insurance agreements, and any other formal or informal agreements.

4. All audit, oversight, or compliance records relating to Flock Safety or its products, including security audits, misuse investigations, and reports submitted to oversight bodies.
5. All records reflecting requests from other law enforcement agencies or private entities for data obtained through Flock products, including but not limited to requests for LPR data.
6. All communications and documents that reference
"Flock" / "Flock Safety," including emails, text messages, PDFs, word processing documents, spreadsheets, presentations, etc.
7. All communications with representatives of Flock Safety (email domain: @flocksafety.com) and any and all reports and data of your audits you have made as an agency yourself or have been subject to by any flock audits (such as the as publicly reported in the Franklin county Citizen. )

Please try to include any other miscellaneous documents that facilitate this municipality's relationship with Flock that don't neatly fall neatly into the above categories.
I am a policy analyst for https://www.shirleyhuman.com/, so the requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. Therefore, I request that any fees are waived. But in the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available. I also respectfully ask that my request is expedited, given the newsworthiness of Flock and its activities.

If you need to contact me, you can reach me at info@ShirleyHuman.com or 706-498-4275. Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.
Sincerely,

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #22-00549-F
communications.communication:
Appeal of DEA FOIA Determination – Case No. 22-00549-F Director Office of Information Policy (OIP) U.S. Department of Justice 441 G Street, NW, 6th Floor Washington, DC 20530 Re: Freedom of Information Act Appeal – Case No. 22-00549-F Dear Director: Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I hereby appeal the DEA’s determination in the above-referenced matter. On August 28, 2025, DEA released 18 pages with extensive redactions under Exemptions 6, 7(C), 7(E), and 7(F). I respectfully submit that the redactions are overly broad and not consistent with FOIA’s foreseeable harm standard, 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(8)(A). Based on the context, the records appear to be a type of log file. Many of the withheld entries reflect employee names or identifiers that may no longer be current given the dated nature of the records. The categorical withholding of such information sweeps far more broadly than necessary to protect legitimate privacy or law-enforcement interests. Specifically: 1. Exemption 6 / 7(C) – The assertion of personal privacy is overextended. Where employees are no longer active or the information is purely professional (e.g., log initials, user IDs), disclosure would not constitute an “unwarranted invasion of privacy.” Courts have consistently held that the mere mention of an employee’s name in the course of official duties does not, standing alone, justify nondisclosure. 2. Exemption 7(E) – The withheld information does not appear to reveal techniques or procedures; instead, the formatting suggests routine entries in an administrative log. Withholding every line item under the theory that it might risk circumvention of the law is unsupported and contrary to FOIA’s narrow construction of exemptions. 3. Exemption 7(F) – There has been no showing that release of employee names or log entries could “reasonably be expected to endanger life or physical safety.” This exemption should not be applied in a blanket manner. DEA’s response letter itself acknowledges the requirement to assess foreseeable harm, yet no explanation was provided beyond citation of exemptions. The Supreme Court and D.C.
Circuit have stressed that agencies must demonstrate with specificity how disclosure would cause harm, not simply recite statutory language. Requested Action: - Conduct a de novo review of the 18 pages. - Release all non-exempt and segregable portions of the log-type records. - Reconsider the application of Exemptions 6, 7(C), 7(E), and 7(F) where entries concern routine employee log data or inactive personnel. - Provide a detailed Vaughn index, or equivalent explanation, that identifies the nature of each redaction and the actual harm anticipated from disclosure. Thank you for your attention to this matter. Please do not hesitate to contact me if additional narrowing of scope would assist in prompt processing. Respectfully submitted, William Fernandes An Open Government Project powered by ChatGPT 127052-94319956@requests.muckrock.com

communications.subject: DC Freedom of Information Act Request: The Phantom Canal: 50-Year Historical Permitting and Stormwater Records for the Unpermitted Waterway Between 1600 and 1490 Morris Rd SE (District Department of Transportation)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

To: DC Department of Buildings (DOB), DC Department of Energy & Environment (DOEE), District Department of Transportation (DDOT) FOIA Officers
Subject: FOIA Request: Historical Permitting, Stormwater Routing, and Earth Disturbance (1600 - 1490 Morris Rd SE)

To the Designated FOIA Officers:

Under the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq.), which establishes that "the public policy of the District of Columbia is that all persons are entitled to full and complete information regarding the affairs of government," I am requesting records pertaining to the lots located between 1600 Morris Rd SE and 1490 Morris Rd SE. 

Please provide copies of the following records dating from January 1, 1976, to the present:
1. All grading permits, earth disturbance permits, and stormwater management plans associated with the creation, excavation, or maintenance of the artificial runoff channel/canal located between these addresses. 
2. All environmental assessments, soil testing reports, and structural shoring plans regarding the slope stability in this specific corridor.
3. All work orders, inspection reports, and violation notices issued for unpermitted municipal runoff diversion, illegal construction, or erosion control failures between 1600 and 1490 Morris Rd SE.
4. All communications (internal and external) regarding the installation of municipal water diversion infrastructure into this wooded area.

Fee Waiver Request:
I request a waiver of all fees associated with this request pursuant to D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b). Disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations or activities of the government, specifically regarding the District's historical oversight of an unpermitted 7-foot by 7-foot artificial canal that has triggered a 25-foot geotechnical slope failure. This failure poses an immediate, unmitigated life-safety hazard along a designated public school student walking route. Furthermore, investigative journalists at WUSA9 are actively reviewing this site and its hazards, ensuring the disclosed information will be broadly disseminated to the public. As a veteran public educator and community advocate, I am seeking these records not for commercial use, but to protect neighborhood safety and ensure regulatory compliance.  DC 311 REQUEST ID 26-00495440 was filed in conjunction with this request on 08/19/2026. 

If my request is denied in whole or part, I ask that you justify all deletions or redactions by reference to specific statutory exemptions. 

Regards,

Fred Gamble Jr.
Ward 8 Resident & Community Advocatece (DGS)

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

communications.subject: DC Freedom of Information Act Request: Duff McCully's Paper Trail: Native GPS Metadata, Urban Forestry Inspection Notes, and Heritage Tree Records for Morris Road SE
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

To: karen.calmeise@dc.gov​

CC: pmendelson@dccouncil.us, callen@dccouncil.gov, trayon.white@dc.gov, ldonovan@wusa9.com, chernande1@wusa9.com, earl.eutsler@dc.gov

SUBJECT: FOIA Request: Comprehensive Historical Records, Leave Designations, and GPS Metadata for Branch Chief Duff McCully (2022–Present)

To the Designated DDOT FOIA Officer,

Under the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq.), I am requesting complete, native-format records—including all electronic correspondence, digital photographs, raw field notes, global positioning system (GPS) location data, and embedded digital metadata—pertaining to Urban Forestry Branch Chief Duff McCully regarding the public right-of-way and corridor between 1600 Morris Rd SE and 1490 Morris Rd SE, dating from March 1, 2022, to the present.

**Please note for processing:** This request is explicitly distinct from, and does not duplicate, my recent FOIA request seeking the field notes of an "unnamed urban forestry professional" who ​unlawful​ly ent​ered  my property in August 2026. This current request strictly targets the historical oversight, administrative communications, and official attendance records of a specific, named executive—Branch Chief Duff McCully—regardless of who was physically dispatched to the site.

Please provide copies of the following specific records in their native metadata formats:

1. All complete field notes, inspection reports, memos, electronic communications, SMS/text messages, and Microsoft Teams chats generated, received, or reviewed specifically by Urban Forestry Branch Chief Duff McCully regarding the corridor, slope failure, and tree health at 1490 and 1600 Morris Rd SE from 2022 to the present (including any historical involvement in the 2022 paper alley tree removal under Work Order wo1075126).
2. All raw GPS tracking data, mobile device inspection logs, geolocated site photographs, and digital metadata associated with any historical field visits conducted specifically by Duff McCully at this location.
3. All official time-and-attendance records, out-of-office designations, and documented medical leave filings for Duff McCully from April 2026 to the present, to verify his administrative availability, deployment logs, and supervisory oversight during this active community hazard.
4. All historical engineering assessments, contractor work orders, and inter-agency routing records tied to municipal stormwater discharge and historical 311 service requests (specifically the 2022 tickets concerning tree mortality and water pooling) that were routed to or managed by Duff McCully's branch.

I request a waiver of all fees pursuant to D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b), as this disclosure directly informs the public regarding an unmitigated life-safety hazard along a public school student walking route, currently under active review by investigative journalists at WUSA9 and the D.C. Council.

Please process this request electronically and provide all native files containing unstripped digital metadata. If any records are withheld or redacted, please justify all deletions by reference to specific statutory exemptions. 

Regards,

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

The FBI's FOIPA Program is searching the FBI's indices for potentially responsive documents.

NOTE: Recent requests are entered into the FOIPA database in the order that they are received. Estimated Dates of Completion

Requests are processed in the order in which they are received through our multi-track processing system, and the FBI receives a voluminous amount of requests on a daily, weekly, monthly, and annual basis. Please check the status of your FOIPA Request at http://vault.fbi.gov by clicking on "Check Status of Your FOI/PA Request" on the right side of the page, and follow the instructions below.



Check the Status of Your FOIPA Request

If your FOIPA Number is [1195846-0] please enter [1195846-000] into the system. If your FOIPA Number is [1195846-1] please enter [1195846-001] into the system. If you have any questions about the status of your FOIPA request, please e-mail foipaquestions@ic.fbi.gov<mailto:foipaquestions@ic.fbi.gov>.



FIND STATUS OF FOIPA- Request statuses are updated weekly



Please enter the whole FOIPA number-Example: [1234567-000]



FOIPA:

Results will show the Request Number, Case Type and Process Description shown below:

FOIPA:

1234567-000



Case Type:

FOIPA



Process Description (Will display the current progress of the request)

The FBI's FOIPA Program is searching the FBI's indices for potentially responsive documents.

You may be contacted via formal letter for all fees and/or negotiation issues that may apply.

NOTE: Recent requests are entered into the FOIPA database in the order that they are received. Before you can check the status, you must have received correspondence assigning a FOIPA request number and the information transferred to the online database. Status information is updated weekly. If a request has been closed within the last six months the online database will display the following: The FOIPA number entered has been closed, and appropriate correspondence has been sent to the address on file.

Estimated Dates of Completion

Requests are processed in the order in which they are received through our multi-track processing system, and the FBI receives a voluminous amount of requests on a daily, weekly, monthly, and annual basis.  Requests are divided into two primary tracks--simple (under 50 pages of potentially responsive documents) and complex (over 50 pages of potentially responsive documents).  Our complex requests are further divided into medium, large, and extra-large sub-tracks.  Simple track requests typically require the least amount of time to process.



Currently, simple track cases average approximately 80 days from the date of receipt for processing.  Requests in the medium processing track are currently averaging 281 days from the date of receipt for processing, those in the large processing track are currently averaging approximately 774 days, and those in the extra-large track are averaging 879 days.


Thank you,



Holly Early
Government Information Specialist
Record/Information Dissemination Section (RIDS)
FBI-Records Management Division
170 Marcel Drive, Winchester, VA 22602-4843
PIO Line: (540) 868-4593
Direct: (540) 868-4854
Fax: (540) 868-4391 or (450)868-4997
Questions E-mail: foipaquestions@ic.fbi.gov<mailto:foipaquestions@ic.fbi.gov>

Electronic FBI FOIPA request submissions are accepted at http://efoia.fbi.gov<http://efoia.fbi.gov/>.

Do you have further questions about the FOIPA process? Visit us at http://www.fbi.gov/foia.

Please check the status of your request online at https://vault.fbi.gov<https://vault.fbi.gov/> by clicking on the "Check Status of Your FOI/PA Request" link on the right side of the page.    Status updates are performed on a weekly basis.

communications.subject: FOIA request 1351761 (A.N.R. Robinson)
communications.communication:
Good afternoon Mr. Delaware,

This is in reference to your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request # 1351761-000 for FBI records concerning A.N.R. Robinson.  We are reaching out to you to determine if you are still interested in these records, or, if at this time, you would consider reducing the size of your request from 1,407 pages to under 950 pages, which will move the request to the medium track.  Reducing the size of your request may accelerate the processing and allow for a more timely receipt of the information you seek, as it could potentially place your request into a smaller, faster processing track.  This may also reduce duplication costs, if applicable.  Currently, there is a significant time involved in processing large track cases.  

Requests are processed in the order in which they are received through our multi-track processing system, and the FBI receives a voluminous amount of requests on a daily, weekly, monthly, and annual basis.  Requests are divided into two primary tracks -simple (under 50 pages of potentially responsive documents) and complex (over 50 pages of potentially responsive documents).  Complex requests are further divided into medium (51-949 pages), (large 950-8000 pages), and extra-large (over 8,000 pages) sub-tracks are based upon request size.

Please contact me with regards to this inquiry to let me know if you are still interested in receiving records for this request either in full (the remaining records), or reducing the request to the medium track (not to exceed 949 pages).  If you reduce the size, you can request the additional records with a new FOIA request upon completion of this one.

Thank you for your time and patience.  We hope to hear from you over the next few days so we can discuss these options.

Best regards,

FOIA Negotiation Team
FBI Information Management Division
540-868-1695

Need a status check? Contact FOIPA Questions (foipaquestions@fbi.gov).

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #1351761-000
communications.communication:
Dear FOIA Negotiation Team-

Hello. Thank you for the message. This reply of mine is in regards to request #: 1351761-000.

Yes, I would like to reduce the size of my request from 1,407 pages to under 950 pages, which will move the request to the medium track. I am hoping to have this request moved into a faster track towards resolution. Please take the steps necessary to move this request to the medium track.

Thank you, I appreciate it.

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #1351761-000
communications.communication:
Will do - thank you for your willingness to reduce the scope of this request.

Best regards,

FOIA Negotiation Team
FBI Information Management Division

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FOIA: DOEE Stormwater Neglect & Downstream Geotechnical Landslides (Morris Rd to Hunter Pl SE)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

To: doee.enforcement@dc.gov; erin.roberts@dc.gov; ouc.foia@dc.gov; ddot.foia@dc.gov

CC: callen@dccouncil.gov; pmendelson@dccouncil.us; twhite@dccouncil.gov; richard.jackson2@dc.gov; brian.hanlon@dc.gov; sharon.kershbaum@dc.gov; david.gadis@dcwater.com; frank.seales@dc.gov; earl.eutsler@dc.gov; duff.mccully@dc.gov; ldonovan@wusa9.com; chernande1@wusa9.com; victoria.fleming@dc.gov

Subject: FREEDOM OF INFORMATION ACT (FOIA) REQUEST: Downstream Stormwater Runoff, Geotechnical Slope Failure, and Drainage Infrastructure (1600 Morris Rd SE to 2216–2258 Hunter Pl SE Corridor)

To the Designated FOIA Officers for DOEE, DOB, OUC (311), DDOT, and DC Water:

Pursuant to the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq.), this is a formal request for public records concerning downstream stormwater impacts, slope erosion, unpermitted earth disturbances, and drainage-related service requests across the continuous geotechnical corridor spanning from 1600 Morris Rd SE to Hunter Pl SE.

I. BASIS OF REQUEST & TOPOGRAPHICAL CORRIDOR
The basis of this request is the continuous topographical slope that originates at the crest of 1600 Morris Rd SE and terminates along the lower elevations and rear boundaries of Hunter Place SE. Stormwater diverted by the unpermitted artificial channel at the ridge line follows gravity through the intervening paper alley and slope profile, impacting private parcels, public easements, and designated student pedestrian corridors downstream.

II. GIS, MAR, AND SSL SEARCH INSTRUCTIONS
To ensure a legally adequate and reasonable search under D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b), FOIA analysts are instructed to utilize the District’s Enterprise GIS / Master Address Repository (MAR) and the OCTO Topographic & Stormwater Catchment data layers. 

Analysts must query the continuous slope corridor using the following spatial and property parameters:
1. Primary Target Addresses: 
   * 2216 Hunter Pl SE
   * 2218 Hunter Pl SE
   * 2220 Hunter Pl SE
   * 2222 Hunter Pl SE
   * 2224 Hunter Pl SE
   * 2226 Hunter Pl SE
   * 2228 Hunter Pl SE
   * 2230 Hunter Pl SE
   * 2232 Hunter Pl SE
   * 2234 Hunter Pl SE
   * 2248 Hunter Pl SE
   * 2258 Hunter Pl SE
   * 1488 Morris Rd SE
   * 1490 Morris Rd SE
   * 1600 Morris Rd SE
2. Intervening Parcels: All Square, Suffix, and Lot (SSL) designations, public rights-of-way, unimproved paper alleys, and municipal easements situated directly between the Morris Road SE crest and the rear lot lines of the Hunter Place SE properties listed above.

III. SCOPE OF REQUESTED RECORDS
Please produce all existing records generated from January 1, 2014, to the present date containing:
1. 311 / OUC Service Requests: All dispatch tickets, service requests, call logs, and inspector resolutions concerning "Yard Flooding," "Drainage Problem," "Standing Water," "Sewer Backup," "Erosion," "Illegal Dumping," "Mudslide," or "Alley Maintenance" for the listed target corridor.
2. DOEE & DC Water Inspections: All illicit discharge evaluations, stormwater runoff investigations, RiverSmart compliance assessments, retaining wall reviews, and soil drainage surveys within the target area.
3. DOB Code Enforcement & Structural Reports: All notices of violation, stop-work orders, structural compromise evaluations, retaining wall permits/citations, or emergency abatement referrals for slope or foundation instability across the specified SSLs.

IV. SEARCH TERMS FOR ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATIONS
In addition to property addresses and SSL identifiers, agency IT and FOIA personnel are directed to execute search queries across agency emails and dispatch databases using the following terms:
* "Hunter Pl"
* "Hunter Place"
* "Morris Rd"
* "Fort Stanton slope"
* "Paper alley"
* "Runoff channel"
* "Slope failure"
* "Soil erosion"
* "Retaining wall"
* "Stormwater diversion"
* "WUSA9"

V. STATUTORY TIMELINE
Under D.C. Official Code § 2-532(c), your respective agencies have fifteen (15) business days to issue a determination regarding this request. As this request seeks to document imminent life-safety and structural hazards affecting public walkways and occupied residences, no unnecessary administrative delay or improper segmentation of this topographical corridor will be accepted.

Please confirm receipt and assign tracking numbers for each agency immediately.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

RE: Public Records Request of August 26, 2026, Reference # R013200-082626 Dear FRED GAMBLE, The District of Columbia received a public records request from you on August 26, 2026. Your request mentioned: To Whom It May Concern: 

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records: 

To: doee.enforcement@dc.gov; erin.roberts@dc.gov; ouc.foia@dc.gov; ddot.foia@dc.gov 

CC: callen@dccouncil.gov; pmendelson@dccouncil.us; twhite@dccouncil.gov; richard.jackson2@dc.gov; brian.hanlon@dc.gov; sharon.kershbaum@dc.gov; david.gadis@dcwater.com; frank.seales@dc.gov; earl.eutsler@dc.gov; duff.mccully@dc.gov; ldonovan@wusa9.com; chernande1@wusa9.com; victoria.fleming@dc.gov 

Subject: FREEDOM OF INFORMATION ACT (FOIA) REQUEST: Downstream Stormwater Runoff, Geotechnical Slope Failure, and Drainage Infrastructure (1600 Morris Rd SE to 2216–2258 Hunter Pl SE Corridor) 

To the Designated FOIA Officers for DOEE, DOB, OUC (311), DDOT, and DC Water: 

Pursuant to the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq.), this is a formal request for public records concerning downstream stormwater impacts, slope erosion, unpermitted earth disturbances, and drainage-related service requests across the continuous geotechnical corridor spanning from 1600 Morris Rd SE to Hunter Pl SE. 

I. BASIS OF REQUEST & TOPOGRAPHICAL CORRIDOR 
The basis of this request is the continuous topographical slope that originates at the crest of 1600 Morris Rd SE and terminates along the lower elevations and rear boundaries of Hunter Place SE. Stormwater diverted by the unpermitted artificial channel at the ridge line follows gravity through the intervening paper alley and slope profile, impacting private parcels, public easements, and designated student pedestrian corridors downstream. 

II. GIS, MAR, AND SSL SEARCH INSTRUCTIONS 
To ensure a legally adequate and reasonable search under D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b), FOIA analysts are instructed to utilize the District’s Enterprise GIS / Master Address Repository (MAR) and the OCTO Topographic & Stormwater Catchment data layers. 

Analysts must query the continuous slope corridor using the following spatial and property parameters: 
1. Primary Target Addresses: 
* 2216 Hunter Pl SE 
* 2218 Hunter Pl SE 
* 2220 Hunter Pl SE 
* 2222 Hunter Pl SE 
* 2224 Hunter Pl SE 
* 2226 Hunter Pl SE 
* 2228 Hunter Pl SE 
* 2230 Hunter Pl SE 
* 2232 Hunter Pl SE 
* 2234 Hunter Pl SE 
* 2248 Hunter Pl SE 
* 2258 Hunter Pl SE 
* 1488 Morris Rd SE 
* 1490 Morris Rd SE 
* 1600 Morris Rd SE 
2. Intervening Parcels: All Square, Suffix, and Lot (SSL) designations, public rights-of-way, unimproved paper alleys, and municipal easements situated directly between the Morris Road SE crest and the rear lot lines of the Hunter Place SE properties listed above. 

III. SCOPE OF REQUESTED RECORDS 
Please produce all existing records generated from January 1, 2014, to the present date containing: 
1. 311 / OUC Service Requests: All dispatch tickets, service requests, call logs, and inspector resolutions concerning "Yard Flooding," "Drainage Problem," "Standing Water," "Sewer Backup," "Erosion," "Illegal Dumping," "Mudslide," or "Alley Maintenance" for the listed target corridor. 
2. DOEE & DC Water Inspections: All illicit discharge evaluations, stormwater runoff investigations, RiverSmart compliance assessments, retaining wall reviews, and soil drainage surveys within the target area. 
3. DOB Code Enforcement & Structural Reports: All notices of violation, stop-work orders, structural compromise evaluations, retaining wall permits/citations, or emergency abatement referrals for slope or foundation instability across the specified SSLs. 

IV. SEARCH TERMS FOR ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATIONS 
In addition to property addresses and SSL identifiers, agency IT and FOIA personnel are directed to execute search queries across agency emails and dispatch databases using the following terms: 
* "Hunter Pl" 
* "Hunter Place" 
* "Morris Rd" 
* "Fort Stanton slope" 
* "Paper alley" 
* "Runoff channel" 
* "Slope failure" 
* "Soil erosion" 
* "Retaining wall" 
* "Stormwater diversion" 
* "WUSA9" 

V. STATUTORY TIMELINE 
Under D.C. Official Code § 2-532(c), your respective agencies have fifteen (15) business days to issue a determination regarding this request. As this request seeks to document imminent life-safety and structural hazards affecting public walkways and occupied residences, no unnecessary administrative delay or improper segmentation of this topographical corridor will be accepted. 

Please confirm receipt and assign tracking numbers for each agency immediately. 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. 

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not. 

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires. 

Sincerely, 

FRED GAMBLE JR 

Upload documents directly: https://www.muckrock.com/respond/2379314/ The District of Columbia has reviewed its files and has located responsive records to your request. Some of the records have been redacted per public records law. Please log in to the DC FOIA Center at the following link to retrieve the responsive records. Public Records Request - R013200-082626  Please know that, under D.C. Official Code §2-537 and 1 DCMR 412, you have the right to appeal this response to the Mayor or to the Superior Court of the District of Columbia.  If you elect to appeal to the Mayor, your appeal must be in writing and contain “Freedom of Information Act Appeal” or “FOIA Appeal” in the subject line of the letter as well on the outside of the envelope.  The appeal must include (1) a copy of the original request; (2) a copy of any written denial; (3) a statement of the circumstances, reasons, and/or arguments advanced in support of disclosure; and (4) a daytime telephone number, and e-mail and/or U.S. Mail address at which you can be reached. 

The appeal must be mailed to: The Mayor’s Correspondence Unit, FOIA Appeal, 1350 Pennsylvania Ave., N.W., Suite 316, Washington, D.C.  20004.  Electronic versions of the same information can instead be e-mailed to The Mayor’s Correspondence Unit at foia.mayor@dc.gov. 

Further, a copy of all appeal materials must be forwarded to the Freedom of Information Officer of the agency involved. Failure to follow these administrative steps will result in delay in the processing and commencement of a response to your appeal to the Mayor. 
Sincerely, Alisoun Hughes

communications.subject: ICE FOIA 2026-ICFO-14329
communications.communication:
01/28/2026 

Andrew Free 
263 Huntington Ave 
Boston, Massachusetts 02115 

RE:	ICE FOIA Case Number 2026-ICFO-14329 
Department of Homeland Security FOIA Case No. 2022-IGFO-00248 
 
Dear Requester: 

This acknowledges receipt of your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to the Department of Homeland Security, dated 7/29/2022, seeking records pertaining to "all communications received by the following email address: "OIGAuditsFollowup@oig.dhs.gov" between January 1, 2022 and the present". 

While processing your request, the Department of Homeland Security located records that fall under the purview of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).  Accordingly, your request was referred to this office for processing and direct response to you.  Your request was received in this office on 1/28/2026. 

Due to the increasing number of FOIA requests received by this office, we may encounter some delay in processing your request.  Per §5.5(a) of the DHS FOIA regulations, 6 C.F.R. Part 5, ICE processes FOIA requests according to their order of receipt.  Although ICE’s goal is to respond within 20 business days of receipt of your request, the FOIA does permit a 10-day extension of this time period.  As the subject matter of your request is of substantial interest to two or more components of this Department or of substantial interest to another agency, we will need to consult with those entities before we issue a final response.  Due to these unusual circumstances, ICE will invoke a 10-day extension for your request, as allowed by Title 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B). We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner. 

We will construe the submission of your request as an agreement to pay up to $25.00. You will be contacted before any further fees are accrued. 

If you have any questions please contact FOIA Public Liaison, Daniel Edgington at 500 12th Street, SW, Washington DC 20536 or (866) 633-1182.  Additionally, you have a right to seek dispute resolution services from the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) which mediates disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies as a non-exclusive alternative to litigation.  If you are requesting access to your own records (which is considered a Privacy Act request), you should know that OGIS does not have the authority to handle requests made under the Privacy Act of 1974.  You may contact OGIS as follows:  Office of Government Information Services, National Archives and Records Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001, e-mail at ogis@nara.gov; telephone at 202-741-5770; toll free at 1-877-684-6448. 

Your request has been assigned reference number 2026-ICFO-14329. Please use this number in future correspondence. 

Sincerely, 

ICE FOIA Office 
Immigration and Customs Enforcement 
Freedom of Information Act Office 
500 12th Street, S.W., Stop 5009 
Washington, D.C. 20536-5009

communications.subject: Florida Sunshine Law Request: Sunshine Law Request: Clearview AI
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Florida Sunshine Law, I hereby request the following records:

- All contracts, licenses, MOUs, MOAs, data agreements, letters of intent, State of Work documents, Scope of Work documents, and other agreement documents with Clearview AI, Inc. that were active any time between 1/1/2023 and the date this request is fulfilled.
- All financial documents or records of financial transactions, exchanges or obligations related to Clearview AI, Inc. Responsive materials include all invoices, bills, receipts, check stubs, or any other records, including those possessed in an electronic format.
- A copy of all training materials, including but not limited to any handouts, workbooks, assessments, presentations, slides, videos, audio files, or other materials, either developed in-house or provided to the agency pertaining to the agency's use of Clearview AI, Inc. products.
- A copy of all agency manuals either developed in-house or provided to the agency pertaining to the agency's use of Clearview AI, Inc. products.
- A copy of all agency policies and procedures either developed in-house or provided to the agency pertaining to the agency's use of Clearview AI, Inc. products.
- A roster of all agency employees who either had or currently have a user account for Clearview AI, Inc. products or had or currently have internal agency permissions to use Clearview AI, Inc. products any time between 7/1/2024 and the date this request is fulfilled.
- A roster of all agency employees who have completed agency training for the use of Clearview AI, Inc. products any time between 7/1/2024 and the date this request is fulfilled.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

e

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: David Joel Horowitz (January 10, 1939 – April 29, 2025)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records mentioning, relating to, or generated as a result of investigation or inquiry into FrontPage Magazine editor David Joel Horowitz (January 10, 1939 – April 29, 2025). His death is widely-known and widely reported; as such, privacy concerns under FOIA Exemptions 6 and 7 are voided, as are any concerns under the Privacy Act. For example, you may find a Fox News report on his death at the following link: https://www.foxnews.com/media/conservative-commentator-david-horowitz-dies-86

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records of both HQ and all field offices for all relevant names, agencies, organizations, companies and events including but not limited to those cited in the previous paragraphs and/or links as well as a cross-reference with the Southern Poverty Law Center to include any information provided by the SPLC. My request includes but is not limited to 137, 157, 176, 177, 183, 184, 188, and 214 files. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

If any part of these documents are exempt from disclosure, please be sure to review and release all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions of responsive documents, as the FOIA requires.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

• All guidelines and regulations regarding the submission and processing of appeals, including but not limited to:
- ­ The appropriate person or position to whom an appeal should be submitted
­ - The appropriate address to which an appeal should be submitted
­ - Any appropriate fax numbers and email addresses available for the submission of appeals ­ All guidelines regarding the processing time and procedures for appeals
­- All rights related to the submission of appeals, including those related to appeal rights for constructive denial

If any part of these documents are exempt from disclosure, please be sure to review and release all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions of responsive documents, as the FOIA requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: South Bay Regional Police Consortium (LA Area) - LexisNexis Data Sharing with Federal LE (Culver City Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

We are working on an article focused on California police departments sharing local data with federal authorities, including ICE via LexisNexis. We identified your agency as part of a South Bay Regional Police Consortium that contracted with LexisNexis for AVCC in or around 2020. This request focuses on data your agency shares with LexisNexis, and interfaces that exist with your agency's RMS/CAD/JMS and LexisNexis's systems, including Accurint, Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC), CommunityCrimeMap.com, or Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEx)

We are requesting:
1) Technical integration documents: Any documents, integrations instructions, tutorials, and similar documents from LexisNexis about how to connect your RMS/CAD/JMS systems to LexisNexis's systems. [Typically held by IT or records systems teams/vendors from when your agency originally integrated with LexisNexis's systems]
2) Agreements: The signed "XML Addendum", Database Interface Agreement, or similar legal agreement that dictates how your agency's data may be used and shared. [Typically held by legal or procurement departments]
3) Shared Data: An export of what data you share with LexisNexis and other law enforcement agencies. This is often called a Data Classification Crime Results sheet. To obtain this, an account admin can click a link on the left-hand side under admin permissions called 'Data Classification Manager.' There is an Export link on the top right of the Data Classification Manager page. Depending on the LexisNexis product(s) you subscribe to, this may have a different name or location. We are looking for the list of data you share with LexisNexis, and who your share it with [Only an CCM/Accurint Account Administrators can access these documents]
4) Occasionally we have found consortiums who have negotiated to only share local data with other consortium members, not the 2,400 AVCC federal and local LE subscribers. If you have documentation that your data is only shared locally, please share it. Otherwise you may state there are no responsive documents to item 4. 

We welcome (but do not expect or request) any comments you have about the sharing of local police data with federal authorities via LexisNexis.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: SFPD Flock Network Searches
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Organization Audit in Flock.
The report should include data logged from the period of August 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Organization Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches done within the agency.

2. Network Audit in Flock.
The report should include data logged from the period of August 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Network Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches of the organization’s Flock network by any agency in the Flock System.

Flock has multiple export options, including the ability to redact or hide certain pieces of data. I am requesting a typical audit export - which should include Org Name, Total Networks Searched, Search Time, Search Reason, Offense Type (if still available, may be associated with older audits), and Text Prompt fields.

These exports should only take several minutes to complete, as I am not requesting officer information, license plate query data, or any other PII. Flock pre-built these audit export functions. If you have any questions please don't hesitate to reach out. 

Best,
Shawn

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

communications.subject: RE: California Public Records Act Request #P266456-072826
communications.communication:
Dear Lt. Polovina,

I'm writing to appeal the redactions applied to the Flock Organization Audit and Network Audit records SFPD has begun producing in response to my request P266456-072826, 7/28/26. This is a rolling production, so this appeal covers everything already sent and everything still to come.

The overwhelming majority of rows reviewed so far includes redactions on five fields: user name, search reason, case number, license plate, and filters. I'm not appealing the name or license plate redactions, those are personal and/or sensitive and I support your need to redact that info. But the blanket redaction of search reason and case number isn't consistent with what I asked for or with a lawful exemption.

My original request specifically named "Search Reason" as a field to produce. Neither reason nor case number identifies a member of the public, and neither is exempt investigative work product; the existence of the search itself was already produced, so SFPD isn't treating the search as confidential, only the stated justification for it.

Under Government Code section 7922.000, SFPD has to justify any withholding with a specific exemption for each redacted field, not a standing practice applied to the export. Under section 7922.525, any reasonably segregable non-exempt information has to be disclosed even when a record contains some exempt material. I've received this same Flock export from more than a dozen other California agencies. None of them redact search reason or case number. If SFPD believes a specific exemption applies here, I'd like to know which one and why it doesn't apply to what comparable agencies in the state is releasing.

To resolve this without further escalation, I'm asking SFPD to:

1. Reissue the records already sent with search reason and case number unredacted.
2. Apply the same standard to the rest of this rolling production going forward.
3. If a specific field is still withheld, cite the applicable Government Code exemption for that field, in writing, per section 7922.000. (only for Reason or Case# if you choose to keep any cells in these columns redacted - all other redactions are good as is - I'm not asking for additional work/justification for those) 

Please provide a substantive response within 15 business days. If the Reason and Case Number redactions stand without a cited legal basis, I reserve the right to file a complaint with the Sunshine Ordinance Task Force and look at a writ of mandate under section 7923.000. I have received millions of rows of data from other agencies, all with the Reason column available for review. I appreciate SFPD's dedication to transparency and hope we can find a reasonable compromise and resolve this redaction issue. 

Thank you,
Shawn Segal

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Electronic copies of the following existing public records of the Second Judicial District Attorney's Office concerning Resilient Solutions 21, Inc. and Axon Enterprise, Inc.:

1. The agreements with Resilient Solutions 21, Inc. dated on or about May 15, 2020 ("IT Development", approximately $275,000), October 16, 2020 ("Develop applications and tools", approximately $755,125), and July 30, 2021 ("Provide license to access software", approximately $64,725), each with all exhibits, statements of work, deliverable and payment schedules, license terms, and amendments.

2. The solicitation or procurement-method records for each of those agreements — the Request for Proposals, Request for Quotes, quotes received, sole-source determination and posting, or statewide price agreement relied upon — including any evaluation or scoring records and the notice of award.

3. Deliverable acceptance records, invoices, and any progress or closeout reports submitted under those agreements.

4. The executed agreements, order forms, or quotes with Axon Enterprise, Inc. for "Justice Premier" software for fiscal years 2026 and 2027 (approximately $363,426 and $467,717), including license counts and pricing.

I do not require the compilation of new records; existing records only. Electronic copies (PDF or native format) are requested. Please advise of any fees before incurring them.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

cassy

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: Skokie Flock ALPR Emails 9-2026
communications.communication:
RE: Skokie Flock ALPR Emails 9-2026

To the FOIA Officer of Skokie Police Department,

This request is made under Illinois Freedom of Information Act. for the following records:

All emails and other written electronic correspondence sent to, received by, or copied ("cc'd" or "bcc'd") to any member of the Village of Skokie Board of Trustees (the Village President and all sitting Trustees, including Trustee Alison Pure Slovin) or to Village Manager John Lockerby, from January 1, 2026 through the date this request is processed, that reference, discuss, or relate to either of the following: "Flock" or "ALPR". Include any attachments to those emails.

For each responsive record, include the sender, all recipients (to/cc/bcc), date, and subject line in addition to the message body, so that correspondence can be attributed to the individual Trustee or the Village Manager who sent or received it. 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

Fee estimates, if any apply, are requested in advance of fulfillment. Electronic delivery is the preferred method of receipt.

A response is anticipated within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

JB_𝗟𝗨𝗖𝗬 𝝦𝝙𝝘𝗦𝝝𝝥𝗦 𝗟𝝙𝝗𝗦

--
BACKGROUND

At the Village of Skokie Board of Trustees meeting on September 8, 2026 (video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RjmNFg15eww), Trustee Alison Pure Slovin (District 2) told the Board that unlike her colleagues, several of whom described hearing concerns from residents about the Village's Flock automated license plate reader (ALPR) program, she had heard privately from constituents in her district who support the Flock cameras. In her words, as recorded in the meeting:

> "...we keep talking about the residents who've reached out to numerous trustees on this board. I'm concerned about these Flock cameras, as everybody said. But I can't speak for the other trustees. But I could tell you that people within the district that I serve, so to speak, have also reached out to me maybe privately and not to all the trustees and have said that they support it because they feel that there is a safety issue and anything that Skokie can do to keep them safe is something that they would commend us on and to continue with. So, you know, we're talking about the few that have reached out to us, but there are the others who are reaching out to us as well. And we have to balance both voices on this board as we move forward. And then if we talk about the amount of people who have reached out to us against Flock cameras, I can't speak for everybody else. It's a dozen people I've heard from. It's not like hundreds of people either. So, you know, we have to really look at who we're representing, what the needs are of this community, and how we help you keep them safe. And the recommendations are from the professionals, and I thank you for that."

Trustee Pure Slovin's comments came during the same September 8, 2026 meeting where the Skokie Police presented on its use of Flock Group ("Flock Safety") automated license plate readers (ALPR), and where numerous Skokie community members spoke during public comment against the Village's Flock ALPR camera network. 

Before public comment began, the board president instituted new decorum rules for the meeting, barring "clapping," "snapping," "standing," or "audible cheers," cast as necessary so that "all positions and voices can be expressed and heard without fear of reprisal." That public comment period then filled to its allotted capacity, roughly ten speakers at three minutes each, and with one exception unrelated to Flock (a labor dispute at a local bakery), every speaker who addressed the Village's Flock/ALPR program spoke against it. No speaker voiced support for Flock or ALPR on the record that night; the only support referenced anywhere in the meeting is the private, secondhand support Trustee Pure Slovin described above. Some quotes from that public comment period:

- "Flock is not an honest company," one commenter said, citing recent contract cancellations in Oshkosh, Wisconsin, and on state-run roads in Texas and Florida: "When I am on the same side as Ron DeSantis, I am embarrassed."
- Another commenter asked how the Village squares its own inclusion and belonging campaigns with "an atmosphere of distrust and fear that is created by flock cameras."
- A third commenter, working through a hypothetical involving a lawful firearm purchase, argued that Flock's camera network could function as a "de facto registry," with every Flock-equipped municipality along a driver's route adding to the trail.
- A commenter who worked through the Skokie Police Department's own case data noted that two of the resulting arrests were for cannabis in an improperly sealed container, not impaired driving, and asked whether those stops would have happened at all without "a false flag in the system."
- A commenter whose work involves information security argued "we can solve crimes without tracking everyone in public," and noted that Flock data collected in Skokie has already been reachable by outside agencies working around Illinois' restrictions on data sharing.
- A commenter affiliated with Lucy Parsons Labs and the Niles Coalition told the Board that the Skokie Police Department's Flock ALPR program has drawn scrutiny as part of "years of work by a coalition of researchers right here in Illinois," documented in a zine published at nilescoalition.org.
- A commenter warned that Flock's AI-enabled search tools mean "you don't really need facial recognition" to identify someone, since the system can be told to find a person matching a plain-language description and "bring in a live feed of that person as they're walking by."
- Another commenter said "there's just no reality on earth that comes to my mind that doesn't make this feel like an Orson Wells novel," adding that discussing "the idea of us living in a surveillance state" with the Board, over cameras that would also watch their own children, was hard to believe.
- A final commenter asked the Board directly how Flock can share footage with law enforcement on request when a homeowner's doorbell-camera network cannot do the same without a subpoena or the owner's consent.

The Lucy Parsons Labs/Niles Coalition commenter also said they had emailed the Board roughly six months earlier, in or around March 2026, with findings on the Skokie Police Department's use of ethnic slurs and its suppression of public ALPR audit logs, and that "nobody has followed up." That unanswered correspondence is part of why this request is being made: it, and any Trustee discussion or response it prompted, should fall within the scope of the records sought above.

During Board discussion of the Flock program, a Trustee referenced haveibeenflocked.com, a third-party tool that lets residents check whether their own license plate data has been captured by Flock cameras, as a resource that could help residents understand the program.

Skokie is one of many Chicago-area and Illinois municipalities where Flock automated license plate reader cameras (also called ALPR or license plate reader cameras) have become a point of public debate, alongside neighboring communities such as Evanston, Lincolnwood, Morton Grove, Wilmette, Winnetka, and Highland Park, and amid a broader statewide and national reckoning with the weapons technology tracked by organizations like Lucy Parsons Labs, the Niles Coalition, and the crowdsourced camera-mapping project DeFlock.org. The only reason Skokie PD, as with those across the country, started taking performative technological reforms was though diligent work by activists. That reckoning though has not slowed Skokie's own program: the Village's Flock cameras were already active by 2023 and remain in place through September 2026, notwithstanding the near-unanimous opposition voiced at the meeting described above. This request is part of an ongoing effort to obtain public records documenting how Flock Group ALPR surveillance technology is adopted and defended by outposts of empire like the Village of Skokie.

communications.subject: Extension Letter
communications.communication:
Dear Requester: 
  
 This email is in response to your recent request, Request Number: 1881-2026 made under the Freedom of Information Act. Section 3(e) of the Freedom of Information Act provides that the five-day response period may be extended for up to five additional working days for a limited number of reasons. Specifically: 
  
 Subsection 3(e)(i) states that the response time period may be extended if “the requested records are stored in whole or in part at other locations than the office having charge of the requested records” 
  
 Subsection 3(e)(ii) states that the response time period may be extended if “the request requires the collection of a substantial number of specified records”. 
  
 Subsection 3(e)(vii) states that the response time period may be extended if "there is a need for consultation, which shall be conducted with all practicable speed, with another public body or among 2 or more components of a public body having a substantial interest in the determination or in the subject matter of the request." 
  
 Pursuant to Subsections 3(e)(i), 3(e)(ii), and 3(e)(vii) we are notifying you of the Village’s intent to extend the time needed to research your request an additional five days. Your FOIA request will be completed no later than Friday, September 25. 
  
 Sincerely, 
  
 Rolando Ithier 
  
 FOIA Officer

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: ILJAOC (CA) - PSDEX/AVCC Contributions and Data Sharing
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1) Foundational Documents: The Accurint Virtual Crime Center 'AVCC XML Addendum' or 'PSDEX Addendum' executed by ILJAOC, including all sub-agency addendums executed by member agencies.

2) Who Contributes: Any documentation, configurations, or records that indicate whether ILJAOC members contribute data to PSDEX/AVCC (Public Safety Data Exchange / Accurint Virtual Crime Center).

3) Who Can Access Agency Data: Any documentation, configurations, or records that indicate what agencies may access contributed data. Specifically, we seek to understand whether ILJAOC members who contribute data to PSDEX/AVCC restrict data access to only ILJAOC members, or if agency data flows into the national PSDEX database available to other AVCC customers.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: ILJAOC (CA) - PSDEX/AVCC Contributions and Data Sharing
communications.communication:
Hi Shawn,

This email will serve as the ILJAOC's preliminary response to your Public
Records Act request identified above. As you are aware, the CPRA generally
provides members of the public with the ability to request inspection or
copies of certain public records. However, an agency’s
obligation to make records available that are responsive to a request does
not require it
to create documents or to compile lists that otherwise do not exist.
Additionally, the
CPRA is not limitless and contains many exemptions from its disclosure
requirements.
In fact, there is no requirement to release an electronic record in its
original format if its
release could result in the disclosure of imbedded data that an agency has
a right, and
potentially a duty, to withhold.

Please note that while prompt access to public records is required by the
CPRA, the
CPRA provides the ILJ 10 days to provide an initial response to the
request. This
correspondence shall serve as the ILJ’s initial response and notification
that the ILJ will
require additional time to make this determination and hereby extends the
deadline to
produce any non-privileged or otherwise protected public records within 14
days of the
date of this letter, or June 15, 2026, as permitted by the CPRA.

To the extent the ILJ possesses responsive records, we will identify,
gather, and
redact such records to exclude all privileged information. The copies of
records responsive
to your request will be provided once the ILJ has had a reasonable time to
locate and review
these records, in PDF format.

If redaction requires preparing a printed copy, copies will be made
available to you
after you pay for the direct cost of duplication. The ILJ will notify you
of the anticipated
total cost for the copies of hard copy documents when all the documents are
compiled.

In the interim, it would help us to best focus the scope of the request if
you can clarify your question. When you ask "who contributes" do you mean
which agencies upload data that is visible to other agencies? And, when you
ask "who can access" do you mean which agencies can access the data of
other agencies? It would help in our search for a responsive document if
you could help clarify these questions. Thank you.

Please do not hesitate to contact me should you have any questions.

Best regards,

Kendra L. Carney Mehr
